name: Jade Costa

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What happens in an ordinary working day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58, play flute for a city chamber group, record passages for dance teachers and teach six adults. I have a music degree and know how to settle a nervous group before its first note. The late train after a rehearsal is dull, but the first clean phrase from a new pupil is lovely.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How does that work fit around home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner works in a library, our children are grown, and we still pay a mortgage. I earn above the usual rate, we have ten months of expenses saved, and several nearby groups use flutes. I use AI occasionally for a draft rehearsal note, then check every name and hour against the signed schedule.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the chamber group that a quicker schedule is welcome if every musician can see the paid rehearsal hours. I would also ask the organiser to write down the late-finish fee.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The chamber season and six pupils are booked, and our ten-month reserve covers a gap between concerts. The mortgage is manageable with the current paid hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This winter I would keep the chamber dates, dance recordings and six pupils, and get written rehearsal and late-finish fees. In the plateau’s first year I would request an actual pension estimate and compare it with our mortgage and health before choosing any retirement date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the present season. A clear fee sheet lets me go home after the last note without wondering what I earned.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What is the late-finish fee for?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A long concert can push me past the cheap train. I want that cost on the same written sheet as the rehearsal.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a pension estimate change your schedule tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. My partner and I need the actual figure first. We have no retirement date on the calendar.

say: I would ask for **visible paid hours** in a quicker schedule.
I would seek a **written late-finish fee** for long concerts.
think: The **booked chamber season** and six paid pupils make this season’s mortgage and ordinary bills manageable.
Our **ten-month reserve** covers a normal gap between concerts without requiring me to take an unpaid date.
do: Keep **chamber dates**, dance recordings and six paid pupils this winter.
Request **written rehearsal fees** and late-finish terms.
Request an **actual pension estimate** in the plateau’s first year and compare it with mortgage and health.
feel: I feel **calm** about booked work and current bills.
S0.quote: A clear fee sheet lets me go home after the last note without wondering what I earned.
fieldNote: Her **booked season**, higher pay and ten-month reserve support a calm plateau.
She seeks an **actual pension estimate** without assuming entitlement or setting a retirement date.

steps.text: Keep booked chamber, recording and six pupil hours this winter
Request written rehearsal and late-finish fees
Request actual pension estimate in first plateau year; compare with mortgage and health

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the dance teachers that generated flute parts can be fast, but a human still has to listen when a pupil runs out of breath. I would ask which recording and teaching hours remain paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Dance recordings make roughly a fifth of my own income. I expect a few buyers to switch to generated parts, though our live concert and pupil work is well booked.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I would ask for written dance recording rates and a paid demonstration of a new AI phrase checker at the music school, which suggests where to breathe in a recorded flute line. In disruption’s first year I would test only my own nameless flute take if the school approves local storage, compare each phrase by ear with the original score, and stop if a breath mark is wrong or the take leaves the school.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing a real slice of my recording income, even with a reserve. I can check a flute recording, but I cannot make a dance teacher buy one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a pupil’s recording go into the checker?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. Their names and playing stay inside the school. My own take is enough to learn whether the checker respects a breath.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the demonstration is unpaid?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for a paid session later. The school should not turn my teaching hour into free testing time.

say: I would ask which **recording hours** still pay.
I would say a **human teacher** hears a pupil’s breath.
think: Some **dance buyers** may leave paid flute recordings.
**Live concerts and pupils** remain booked, though they do not erase a lost fifth.
do: Request **written recording rates** and a paid phrase-checker demonstration next month.
Test the **phrase checker** after paid instruction and approved local storage on my nameless take; compare by ear, stop errors/leaks.
feel: I feel **anxious** about plausible recording losses.
S1.quote: I can check a flute recording, but I cannot make a dance teacher buy one.
fieldNote: Her **new phrase checker** requires paid instruction, approved storage, owned nameless audio and manual breath checks.
The **dance-recording fifth** is exposed despite well-paid live and teaching work.

steps.text: Request written dance rates and paid phrase-checker lesson next month
Test checker after paid lesson/local approval using own nameless take; compare breath marks, stop errors/leaks

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell our group that thinking AGI by 2028 could make dance recordings before a robot can play flute around 2031. I would ask for the live player fees in writing now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the dance recording work to end in 2028, removing a fifth of my own pay. The live chamber calls and pupils may hold, but I will not assume every venue keeps its budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would total dance invoices and request signed chamber and pupil hours. In the first year after 2028, if recordings end and paid live hours also fall, I would apply for a posted paid community music tutor role only if the employer accepts my music degree and adult teaching record, its written net pay after travel replaces the lost fees and the last train fits; I would keep current chamber and pupil work until a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the expected recording loss, but ten months saved and nearby jobs let me compare real offers. I would be much more worried if live hours fell too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a human tutor still do?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would hear a new player strain on a high note and change the exercise in the room. I already teach adults, but a new employer must actually post and pay for that work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why does 2028 matter before 2031?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Thinking AGI can price down a recording in 2028. The card places hands-on instrument robots about three years later.

say: I would request **written live fees** now.
I would separate **2028 AGI** from robot flute playing around 2031.
think: I expect **dance recordings** to end in 2028.
A further **live-hour cut** would make a new paid role worth checking.
do: Total **dance invoices** and request signed chamber and pupil hours now.
Apply for **posted music tutor** after recording/live losses if degree and teaching qualify; require written replacement net after travel.
Keep **chamber and pupils** until signed offer and workable last train.
feel: I feel **anxious** about expected recording loss with room to compare offers.
S2.quote: I would hear a new player strain on a high note and change the exercise in the room.
fieldNote: The **2028 recording loss** precedes robot flute players around 2031.
A **human tutor opening** needs accepted degree and adult teaching, written net replacement, train access and signed offer.

steps.text: Total dance invoices and request signed chamber/pupil hours now
Apply after recording/live losses to posted tutor role accepting degree/teaching; written replacement net after travel
Keep paid chamber and pupils until signed offer; check last train

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the school that five years until AGI by 2031 lets us see whether adults will pay for a small flute circle. I would say the fee has to cover a clean instrument and a paid accompanist.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Dance buyers may thin gradually by 2031. A separate adult circle could replace some fees, but I will not raid our ten-month bill reserve for a room no one has booked.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This spring I would test interest outside my booked chamber calls and pupils, then get the room booking and its hire charge in writing before taking deposits. I would start a six-week flute circle only after eight adults prepay enough for my teaching and preparation, a paid accompanist, that room charge, inspected and cleaned flute hire and train fares; in the first year after 2031 I would renew only at that full eight-place floor, replacing unsafe flutes or deferring and refunding the whole group if eight safe paid places cannot remain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the possible dance-fee slide, but I can test a paid circle without gambling the reserve. Eight flute-class fees must pay the accompanist before anyone calls the class my new income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if only five adults sign up?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would refund all five deposits and keep my booked chamber calls. Five fees do not cover two workers and the room.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if a hired flute is unsafe or unclean?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would get a safe cleaned replacement before class. If eight safe paid places cannot remain, I would defer and refund everyone.

say: I would test **adult demand** for a separate flute circle.
I would price **clean instruments** and a paid accompanist into the fee.
think: **Dance buyers** may thin before 2031, reducing the income I get from recording flute passages for teachers.
Our **ten-month reserve** belongs to household bills, so an unbooked room cannot be charged against it.
do: Keep **booked chamber calls** and pupils while testing demand this spring.
Book **written room charge** before deposits; require eight fees covering room, own teaching/prep, accompanist, safe cleaned flute hire and travel.
Renew **after 2031** at the full floor; replace unsafe flutes or defer and refund whole group below eight safe places.
feel: I feel **anxious** about dance fees while checking a paid alternative.
S3.quote: Eight flute-class fees must pay the accompanist before anyone calls the class my new income.
fieldNote: The **eight-place floor** covers her teaching and preparation, paid accompanist, written room, clean safe hire and trains.
Low **enrolment or unsafe flutes** require safe replacement or whole-group deferral and refund.

steps.text: Keep booked chamber and pupils while testing adult demand
Book written room charge before fees; eight deposits cover room, teaching, prep, accompanist, safe hire, travel
Replace unsafe flutes or defer and refund whole group below eight safe paid places
Renew after 2031 only when eight safe fees cover all wages, prep, room, hire, travel

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the chamber group that a decade until AGI by 2036 is time to put rehearsal, teaching and preparation fees in writing. Robot flutes around 2039 are a later issue than today’s paid calls.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 68 I might want fewer late trains, but I have not seen a pension figure and have no retirement date. Live concerts and pupils pay well now; recorded dance parts might be gone by 2036.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I would request an actual pension estimate and written chamber renewal, then save one tenth of each extra paid concert fee after mortgage, food and train fares toward twelve months of expenses. Across the decade I would launch the separate flute circle on free Saturdays outside booked chamber calls, only after the room booking and hire charge are written down before deposits and eight safe paid places cover my teaching and preparation, a paid accompanist, room charge, cleaned instrument hire and travel. In the first year after 2036 I would renew only on that same full-cost eight-place floor while keeping paid chamber calls and pupils, replacing unsafe flutes or deferring and refunding the whole group if eight safe paid places cannot remain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about distant recording changes while current live and teaching income holds. I will not count an unknown pension or an unfilled flute class as pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no extra concert fee arrives?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then the reserve gets nothing new from concerts. Twelve months is a goal, not a balance we already have.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you stop playing at 68?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. My partner and I would weigh the actual estimate, our health and paid bookings. A birthday does not settle the mortgage.

I would separate **2036 AGI** from robot flutes around 2039.
think: Our **live and pupil income** pays well now, leaving the next season’s mortgage covered.
An **unknown pension** cannot choose my retirement date, even if I want fewer late trains at 68.
do: Keep **paid chamber/pupils**; request actual pension estimate/renewal; save 10% of extra paid concerts after bills/trains toward twelve months.
Launch **flute circle** after written room charge before deposits; eight fees cover room, own teaching/prep, accompanist, safe cleaned hire, trains.
Renew **after 2036** on the same full eight-place floor; replace unsafe flutes or defer and refund whole group.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about distant recording loss while current paid work holds.
S4.quote: I will not count an unknown pension or an unfilled flute class as pay.
fieldNote: Her **twelve-month target** uses only extra paid concert fees after mortgage, food and train costs.
The **2036 renewal** preserves eight safe places paying both workers, preparation, room and hire/travel, or refunds the whole group.

Save tenth of extra concert fees after bills/travel toward twelve months
Launch circle after written room charge; eight fees cover room, teaching, prep, accompanist, safe hire, trains
Renew after 2036 at full eight-place floor; replace unsafe flutes or defer/refund whole group

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because paid dance recordings could end quickly, even with a good live calendar. Signed chamber hours, a real tutor vacancy accepting my degree and written net pay after travel would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who cleans a hired flute before a beginner lifts it. An instrument must be safe and paid for before I call eight deposits a class.

headlineQuote: An instrument must be safe and paid for before I call eight deposits a class.
portrait: Jade is a **58-year-old flutist** with a music degree, chamber work, dance recordings and six adult pupils.
Her **higher pay**, ten-month reserve and many nearby groups secure current income while recordings face risk.
She uses **AI occasionally** and trials a new phrase checker only after paid instruction, approved storage and manual listening.
Her **adult flute circle** requires eight safe prepaid places covering teaching/prep, accompanist, room, clean hire and travel.
biggestWorry: The **2028 scenario** could end dance recordings quickly, despite a well-booked live calendar.
whatWouldHelp: She needs **signed chamber hours**, a posted tutor vacancy accepting her degree and written replacement net after travel.
